LESSON: READING 15.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: POEMS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.4: Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to relate ideas read in works of art to real life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain why it is important to relate ideas learnt in poems to real life
2. identify the key elements of an email
3. apply the elements in writing an email
4. appreciate the importance of writing emails

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 15.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: POEMS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 15.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: POEMS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Explain why it is important to relate ideas learnt in poems to real life

What this means
In this part you learn to explain why it is important to relate ideas learnt in poems to real life. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain why it is important to relate ideas learnt in poems to real life.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain why it is important to relate ideas learnt in poems to real life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Identify the key elements of an email

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the key elements of an email. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the key elements of an email.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the key elements of an email. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Apply the elements in writing an email

What this means
In this part you learn to apply the elements in writing an email. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply the elements in writing an email.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply the elements in writing an email. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the importance of writing emails

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of writing emails. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of writing emails.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of writing emails. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: explain why it is important to relate ideas learnt in poems to real life)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems to a partner. (skill: identify the key elements of an email)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: apply the elements in writing an email)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: appreciate the importance of writing emails)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain why it is important to relate ideas learnt in poems to real life.
3. Practise this skill: identify the key elements of an email.
4. Practise this skill: apply the elements in writing an email.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to relate ideas read in works of art to real life?
2. What is the role of poems in the society?
3. Why do we write emails?
4. What is the difference between emails and letters?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain why it is important to relate ideas learnt in poems to real life.
5. Be able to: identify the key elements of an email.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
